title: JSON lane transport for program-to-program calls

claims.text: The document defines lineage.family/1 as a strict recipient-owned transport where stdio reads one JSON object to EOF and writes one canonical receipt plus LF.
The public layout table fixes family/<Endpoint>/config.json, consumer.lock, spool requests, state results with .done sentinels, quarantine entries and dedup retention.
The request rules cap raw input at 65536 bytes, bound integers to the safe-integer range, limit nesting to 64 levels, and reserve id invalid0 for unidentifiable receipts.
The worked examples show capabilities, events.read with an exclusive after cursor, and a call retry that returns the original commit without appending another event.

triggers: duplicate request id with different payload

decision.rule: Change here when the family envelope shape, mailbox layout, request bounds or retry deduplication needs to change.
decision.failure: Unsafe configuration is accepted, an exact retry appends a second event, or a changed payload under a retained id is not refused.

questions.q: Where is the family mailbox layout and its .done sentinel documented?
Where should I change the raw request byte cap and integer bounds?
Where can I debug why a JSON lane request is refused with bad_args?
Why does an exact retry of a published request return the original commit?
